input: Research 529 college savings plans for kids

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of children, their ages, and who the account owner will be affects which plan types, contribution timelines, and beneficiary structures make the most sense.

The user may want a broad overview of how 529s work, or they may already understand the basics and need a deep comparison of specific plans — this completely changes the depth and direction of the research.
The monthly or lump-sum amount they can contribute determines which plans' minimums, fee structures, and investment options are relevant or off the table.

The state the user lives in matters enormously — many states offer tax deductions only for their own state's plan, which could make an in-state plan the default best choice regardless of other factors.
Some people want a hands-off age-based portfolio; others want to self-direct investments. This determines which plan features and fund options to prioritize in the research.
What the user wants to walk away with — a shortlist of 2-3 plans, a comparison spreadsheet, a final single recommendation — defines how the research should be packaged and when it is done.
Knowing whether the user plans to open the account themselves online or work with a financial advisor determines whether to focus on direct-sold vs. advisor-sold plans.

gold.taskTitle: Research 529 college savings plans for kids
gold.taskDescription: Investigate 529 college savings plan options to make an informed decision about saving for a child's or children's future education costs.

questions.title: How many kids are you saving for, and how old are they?
questions.description: Identify the number of children and their current ages to shape the investment timeline and whether separate accounts or a single beneficiary account makes sense.

questions.title: Do you want a basic overview or a deep plan comparison?
questions.description: Determine whether the user needs foundational education on how 529s work or is ready to evaluate and compare specific plan options.

questions.title: What state do you currently live in?
questions.description: Identify the user's state of residence, since state tax deduction eligibility is often the single biggest factor in choosing a plan.

questions.title: How much do you expect to contribute monthly or upfront?
questions.description: Understand the contribution budget to filter plans by minimum investment requirements and assess which fee structures will have the most impact.

questions.title: Do you prefer a hands-off portfolio or self-directed investing?
questions.description: Clarify the user's investment style preference to determine whether age-based automatic portfolios or flexible self-directed fund options should be prioritized.

questions.title: What should this research produce — a shortlist, a comparison, a single pick?
questions.description: Define the desired output so the research has a clear endpoint and the right level of detail.

questions.title: Will you open the account yourself online or use a financial advisor?
questions.description: Determine the intended account-opening method to focus research on direct-sold plans (DIY) versus advisor-sold plans, which differ in fees and availability.
